what: edited/check3/c3-b.test.ts ('an Equal key held...'): The note says zoom from wheel or keys travels about the same at 30 and 60 fps. That holds for one wheel step (log zoom 0.201 against 0.202). A held Equal key adds its step once per frame, so the same half-tenth of a second held zooms about twice as far at 60 fps as at 30 fps (log 5.41 against 2.71). True words: "one wheel step travels about the same at 30 and 60 fps; a held zoom key adds its input once per frame, so it zooms further at a higher frame rate".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n05'): The note says a new target object is still used as long as the view has not been built since the last change. But any read of worldMatrix (getCameraPosition, a child, the renderer) builds the local matrix too: after alpha = 1.2 and getCameraPosition, a new target object is ignored even though getViewMatrix never ran. True words: "once worldMatrix has been read after the last change (getViewMatrix, getCameraPosition and the like)".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n17/n50'): The note says field writes to a hand-made ortho object show only once fov, nearPlane, farPlane, the aspect or the view changes. A field write to the bounds that enableOrthographicCamera returned earlier for that camera also makes it show, even when that object is no longer camera.ortho, because the old setter still invalidates the camera (halfHeight 3 shows after own.halfHeight = 7). True words: add "or a field write to any bounds object enableOrthographicCamera returned for that camera".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n17/n50'): The note says a hand-set bounds object is used 'else once fov, nearPlane, farPlane, the aspect or the view changes'. A changing write to a field of the bounds enableOrthographicCamera returned earlier for that camera brings it in as well, with none of those changed. True words: "...or the view changes, or a field of bounds enableOrthographicCamera returned for that camera is written".

edited/check3/c3-c.test.ts: The note says that for beta outside (0, PI) the pans flip where sin(beta) < 0, and go along world +X/+Y only at beta = PI. At beta = 2*PI (sin is -2.4e-16) the frame step moves the target +X and +Y (0.01, 0.01, 0), the same as at PI, not a flipped beta-0 move. True words: "where |sin(beta)| < 1e-10 and beta is not exactly 0 (PI, 2*PI, -PI) they go along world +X and +Y".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n13'): The note says flyGeospatialCameraToAsync resolves at its end, at a newer flight or after control input. Its end only comes from frames, so after disposeScene clears _beforeRender mid-flight the promise stays pending for good (it settles only if a newer flight starts). True words: "it resolves only while the scene runs frames: at its end, ...; if the scene is disposed mid-flight it stays pending".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n08'): The note says a changing write between its frames cancels it. A write that changes alpha and is undone before the next frame does not cancel it, because only the pose at the next frame is compared (it resolves). True words: "it rejects if at a later frame the pose differs from what it last wrote; a change undone before that frame does not cancel it".

edited/check3/c3-b.test.ts ('n61'): The note says that after a pan or zoom stops, center moves to where the look vector from the eye hits the planet sphere. With the eye inside the sphere (center at |c| = 5e5 on a 1e6 planet) the look ray does hit the sphere, on the far side, but nothing moves: the re-centre only takes a hit the eye looks down onto. True words: "...hits the planet sphere from outside; if the ray misses or the eye is inside the sphere, nothing moves".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n35'): The note says writing upVector rolls the camera unless it is parallel to the view direction. Setting it to (0, 0, 0) on a camera looking along +X also gives the identity rotation and turns the camera to look along +Z. True words: "unless it is zero or parallel to the view direction".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n23'): The note says the frame step never takes radius below 0.01. With setCameraLimits upperRadiusLimit 0.005 the step writes max(0.01, r) and the setter then clamps it to 0.005, so radius ends below 0.01. True words: "...never take radius below 0.01 unless an upperRadiusLimit below 0.01 is set".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n29'): The note says the pinch sets radius to at least 0.01. With upperRadiusLimit 0.005 set through setCameraLimits, the pinch leaves radius at 0.005, because the limit clamp runs after the 0.01 floor. True words: "at least 0.01, unless an upperRadiusLimit below that is set".

edited/check3/c3-a.test.ts ('n03'): The note says that while setCameraLimits is active, a write that changes alpha, beta or radius re-clamps all three. A NaN write is not clamped: radius = NaN stays NaN under lowerRadiusLimit 5 and upperRadiusLimit 20, because NaN fails both comparisons. True words: "re-clamps every channel that is below or above a set limit; NaN is left as it is".

Note 7 says each key move or drag on attachFreeControl/attachConfigurableFreeControl puts target 1 unit ahead along _yaw/_pitch and replaces a hand-set target. Note 36 says these controls given no scene never move the camera, because all motion happens in _beforeRender. For a drag on a scene-less free control, the reader cannot tell whether the drag still rewrites target/_yaw (note 7) or does nothing (note 36). Note 1 says scene-less arc-rotate drags do reach the camera's offset fields, so the reader may guess wrong either way.

"Each clamp ... zeroes only the inertial offset of the channel that hit a bound". Broad reading: this also covers attachControl's frame-step beta clamp to [0.01, PI-0.01] (note 10), the 0.01 radius floor (notes 23, 29) and interpolateArcRotateCamera's goal clamp (note 51), so beta hitting 0.01 zeroes inertialBetaOffset. Narrow reading: only the setCameraLimits clamps (note 3), and the frame-step clamps leave the offsets alone, so rotation keeps pushing against the bound.

Note 3 (setCameraLimits re-clamps to the limit fields) and note 10 (attachControl's frame step clamps beta to [0.01, PI-0.01] only on rotating frames; there are no beta limits by default). With lowerBetaLimit below 0.01 or upperBetaLimit above PI-0.01, the reader cannot tell which bound wins on a rotating frame. The same question applies to lowerRadiusLimit below 0.01 against the 0.01 floor in note 23.

"attachControl acts only on button 0 (rotate) and 2 (pan)". Read as fixed, the parenthetical says button 0 always rotates. The same note then says pointerMappings apply to mouse and pen, so primaryButton:'pan' makes button 0 pan. A reader who takes the parenthetical at its word ignores pointerMappings. It is only the default.

"A right-drag of (dx, dy) px adds ... to inertialPanningX/Y". Broad reading: every right-drag pans. Narrow (true per notes 19 and 39): only a drag mapped to 'pan', which is the right button by default; with secondaryButton:'rotate' a right-drag rotates and with primaryButton:'pan' a left-drag pans. Note 39 correctly says "A rotate drag"; note 24 should say "a pan drag".

Notes 24 and 39 give the sign of horizontal pan (-dx/panningSensibility) and of alpha (subtract dx/angularSensibility) with no build named. Note 69 says a right-handed build (babylon-lite-rh) flips both. A reader who uses note 24 or 39 alone in an RH build gets the sign wrong. Note 44 names the RH case inline; 24 and 39 do not.

Note 57 says yaw PI/2 (east) heads toward -Y at a center on +X, with no build named. Note 70 says that in a right-handed build east, and so yaw PI/2, points toward +Y. A reader who reads 57 alone applies -Y in both builds.

"Writes to the original target's x/y/z show at once." Reading 1: x/y/z writes in place on whatever camera.target currently is show at once. Reading 2: they show only on the object createArcRotateCamera made, even after a new object was assigned; then the original is no longer camera.target, and it is unclear whether writing to it does anything. After target = newObj, the reader cannot tell whether newObj.x = 1 or oldObj.x = 1 shows, or whether both are missed.

Note 5 says an assigned target object and writes to it show only at the next changing alpha/beta/radius write. Note 24/25 say each frame a pan moves the target, and note 51 says interpolateArcRotateCamera writes goal.target to camera.target. Two cases are left open. After target was reassigned, does an attachControl pan, or a target-only interpolation (no alpha/beta/radius change), show in the view? And does the interpolation write in place or assign a new object? The reader cannot tell which note governs.

"The frame step and the pinch never take radius below 0.01; a direct write can." Reading 1: every frame step clamps radius to >= 0.01, so a radius of 0.001 written directly is raised at the next frame. Reading 2: only a zoom step (inertialRadiusOffset non-zero) is floored, and a written 0.001 stays, as beta = 0 does in note 10. Code that writes radius directly behaves differently under each reading.

"overwritten in place on the next change (or other aspect)". Reading 1: the returned matrix object updates as soon as the camera changes, so a held reference follows the camera with no getter call. Reading 2: it is overwritten only when a getter is next called after a change. The note does not say whether the overwrite happens at the camera write or at the next getViewMatrix/getProjectionMatrix call, nor which changes count.

Note 43 says a new object assigned to camera.limits is read live by attachGeospatialControls for zoom, the pick sphere and the collision floor, but is ignored by the camera's own clamps, the controls' re-centre included. Note 61 says the re-centre moves center to where the look ray hits "the planet sphere". The reader cannot tell whether that sphere's radius comes from the camera's original limits.planetRadius or from the assigned object (the pick sphere, which note 43 says is live).

Note 3 says that while setCameraLimits is active, any changing alpha/beta/radius write is re-clamped. Notes 37 and 51 say interpolateArcRotateCamera follows the shortest arc and clamps only its goals. Note 8 says it rejects if a value differs from what it last wrote. Case: limits alpha [0, 6.2], from 0.1 to a goal of 6.0. The shortest arc passes below 0. The reader cannot tell whether the intermediate write is clamped (and if so whether the promise then rejects under note 8) or whether interpolation is exempt.

"is moved to +-87.13 when applied (center assignment, setGeospatialOrientation, or the next yaw/pitch/radius write ...)". Reading 1: the list is complete, so an attachGeospatialControls pan or key pan toward the pole, or the re-centre in note 61, is not limited. Reading 2: every way the center is applied, controls included, is limited. The note also does not say whether camera.center itself reads back the moved value.

Note 26 says createGeospatialCamera starts at radius 4*planetRadius with no exception. Notes 9 and 27 say it starts at 10 when 4*planetRadius < 10. A reader of note 26 alone uses the wrong start radius for a small planet.

"arrows pan the center north/east by up to radius*0.0015 per frame". The note does not say what makes the step smaller. Reading 1: radius*0.0015 is the fixed step per frame. Reading 2: some unstated factor (frame time, distance, ramp-up) scales it down. A reader computing a pan distance cannot choose.

"attachControl's keyboard option is ignored unless enableArcRotateKeyboardControls() ran first". Two scopes are open. "First" may mean before this attachControl call, or before the keys are pressed. And it is not said whether keyboard left undefined turns keys on or off once the module is enabled. A reader may omit the option and expect keys, or call enable after attaching and expect it to apply.

"by the radius asked for, before radiusMin/radiusMax clamp it". For a pitch-only write, "the radius asked for" could be the current radius or the last radius requested before clamping. For a radius-only write, it is not said whether pitch is re-clamped against the new radius. The reader cannot tell whether writing radius after pitch re-limits the pitch they already set.

"cssX/cssY = x*cssWidth/backingWidth, y*cssHeight/backingHeight". The note does not cover the case where neither cssWidth nor cssHeight is given (both are optional). Reading 1: cssX equals x. Reading 2: cssX is NaN or undefined.

Note 17 says field writes to a hand-made ortho bounds object show once fov, nearPlane, farPlane, the aspect or the view changes. Note 50 says a hand-set bounds object is ignored entirely (perspective is used) until enableOrthographicCamera has run once on some camera. A reader of note 17 alone expects a hand-made object to work after a fov change even when enableOrthographicCamera never ran.

"fov is ignored" under ortho. Broad reading: writing fov has no effect at all. Note 66 says a fov write still rebuilds the projection, so a pending hand-set ortho takes effect. Only fov's value is unused. A reader who takes "ignored" broadly will not use a fov write to force a rebuild, and will not expect a fov write to change what is rendered.

"crossed limits make the clamp recurse into a RangeError". The note does not say when this throws. Reading 1: the setCameraLimits call itself throws. Reading 2: it throws at the next changing alpha/beta/radius write, which may be inside an attachControl frame step or an interpolation. Where a reader puts a try/catch depends on which.

"Each key move or drag puts target 1 unit ahead". Reading 1: only frames with key or drag input. Reading 2: every frame on which the move or turn velocity is non-zero, so glide frames after release (notes 34, 46) also overwrite a target set by hand during the glide.
